QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_66

question.text: Under SAS-1300 the BHIM / UPI / PayTM digital-payment adoption indicator should be verified using:

answer.text: NPCI aggregated district-wise UPI volume + partner-bank transaction logs + beneficiary demo-day proof + sub-sample 6-month-later check

explanation.text: The Logic: Verification of digital-payment adoption is strongest when it combines independent sources: aggregated NPCI district-wise UPI volume (sector-level benchmark), partner-bank transaction logs (individual-level evidence of actual usage), demo-day proof (evidence of skill acquisition), and a later sub-sample retention check (evidence of sustained behaviour). Triangulating these sources is more robust than any single source. The Trap: Option B uses only the SE's internal data with no independent corroboration. Options C ('an ad') and D ('a TV interview') are promotional materials, not evidence of usage. Note: The specific NPCI district-wise UPI volume, partner-bank transaction logs, demo-day proof and six-month retention-check combination is not described in the cited Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) at pages 181-182, 130, 215 or 102. The workbook supports BHIM/UPI/PayTM as session content and identifies beneficiaries, partner FIs and banks/NBFCs, interviews/questionnaires, the 8% sample, and desk-review data as evidence sources. The framing above reflects general industry knowledge of digital-payment adoption verification.
